courses.title: AP World History: Modern
courses.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
courses.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

previewTopics.title: East Asia
previewTopics.summary: Song China: an enduring government, changing economy, and influential culture.

previewTopics.title: Dar al-Islam
previewTopics.summary: Regional Muslim states, connected communities, and the movement of ideas across Afro-Eurasia.

previewTopics.title: South and Southeast Asia
previewTopics.summary: Hindu, Buddhist, and Muslim communities; inland kingdoms and maritime states.

courses.title: AP Precalculus
courses.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
courses.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

previewTopics.title: Change in Tandem
previewTopics.summary: How input values and output values of a function vary together: domain and range, increasing and decreasing, concavity, and zeros.

previewTopics.title: Rates of Change
previewTopics.summary: Average rates of change over intervals, rates of change at a point, and what the sign of a rate of change says about how two quantities vary together.

previewTopics.title: Rates of Change in Linear and Quadratic Functions
previewTopics.summary: Average rates of change for sequences, linear functions, and quadratic functions, secant lines, and how the change in average rates of change reveals concavity.

courses.title: AP U.S. History
courses.description: Trace how Americans have argued over identity, power, work, and their place in the world, from the societies that existed before 1491 to the present.
courses.previewDescription: Follow the nation's development from early contact and colonization through independence, civil war, industrialization, world wars, and recent decades.

previewTopics.title: Contextualizing Period 1
previewTopics.summary: What a historical context is, and the Native American, European, and African developments that framed the encounters of 1491 to 1607.

previewTopics.title: Native American Societies Before European Contact
previewTopics.summary: How maize, aridity, mixed farming, and ocean resources shaped the economies and settlements of Native American societies across North America before 1491.

previewTopics.title: European Exploration in the Americas
previewTopics.summary: Why Spain, Portugal, England, and France sent ships across the Atlantic: wealth, rivalry among monarchies, and the spread of Christianity.
